question: A sales manager wants to know which reps logged the most calls this month. Which report type should they use?
explanation: Use Tasks and Events. It pulls calls, meetings, and tasks for everyone in the org, so the manager can see call counts by rep.
whyWrong: Activities with Accounts and Accounts with Activities are about account-level activity, not calls per rep.
Activity History is just a list on a record page. It isn't a report type you can build this report from.

question: With standard field history tracking, how many fields can an administrator track per object?
explanation: 20. That's the cap, on every standard or custom object.
whyWrong: 20 is the real number, so 10, 15, and 25 are all wrong.

question: Which separate system permission is built for transferring multiple records in bulk?
explanation: Transfer Records. It lets a user hand off records they don't own to someone else.
whyWrong: View All just grants read access, it doesn't let anyone move ownership.
Modify All is broad and can touch ownership too, but Transfer Records is the dedicated permission built for bulk transfers.
Edit lets you change records you can already reach. It doesn't give you rights over records you don't own.

question: A company wants an AI agent to answer common customer questions from approved company info, and hand off anything complicated to a person. What should the administrator configure?
options: Agentforce with an appropriate topic and actions
A scheduled Flow that runs once each day
A dashboard with a filtered report
A validation rule on the Case object
explanation: Agentforce, set up with the right topic and actions. Give it proper guardrails and a handoff path for anything it can't safely answer.
whyWrong: A scheduled Flow just runs at a set time. It can't hold a conversation with a customer.
A dashboard shows report data. It doesn't respond to anyone.
A validation rule only checks data on save, it can't answer questions or route a conversation.

question: Which record-triggered flow option runs before a record is saved?
explanation: Before Save. It runs before the record hits the database, so it can update or check fields on the way in.
whyWrong: A Platform Event flow kicks off from an event message, that's a different trigger entirely, not a before-save timing option.
After Save runs once the record is already saved, too late to change fields before that save.
After Delete fires once a record is gone. It has nothing to do with saving a record.

question: Which feature lets an admin change the components shown on a Home page?
explanation: Lightning App Builder. Use it to add and arrange components on a Home page.
whyWrong: Validation rules check what gets entered into a record, they have nothing to do with Home page layout.
Record types control which picklist values and layouts a record gets. They don't touch the Home page.
Profiles control access and settings, not what shows up on Home. That's Lightning App Builder's job.
examDomain: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

question: What can sales managers learn from a Campaign Influence report?
options: Campaigns that influenced opportunities and closed revenue
explanation: It shows which campaigns actually influenced opportunities, and how much of that closed revenue they can take credit for.
whyWrong: Email open rates are a separate marketing metric, not what Campaign Influence reports on in Sales Cloud.
Campaign Influence ties campaigns to revenue, it isn't limited to spend.
Lead source counts won't tell you which campaigns moved opportunities forward.

question: Which criteria options can a Case assignment rule use?
options: Both rule criteria and formula criteria
explanation: Both. You can build criteria from fields or from formulas.
whyWrong: Assignment rules support formulas too, not just field-based criteria.
They support field-based criteria too, not just formulas.
Manual assignment isn't a criteria type at all, it's just what happens when no rule catches the case.

question: Why assign cases to a queue?
options: Give a team a shared list of cases to claim or work
explanation: So a team has one shared pool of work to pull from. Assignment rules or other routing can feed cases into that queue.
whyWrong: Queues route and share work. Reporting is a separate feature.
A queue might send a notification, but its real job is giving a team a shared list to work.
Queues organize work, they don't delete anything.

question: Which records provide the product catalog and pricing that can be added to an opportunity?
explanation: Products define what the company sells. Price books and their entries set the prices you can actually use on an opportunity.
whyWrong: Leads matter earlier in the sales process, but they don't carry product or price book data.
Campaigns track marketing activity. You don't need one to add products and pricing to an opportunity.
Opportunities are where products and price books get used, but they aren't the source of the product data itself.

question: Which report format groups data by both rows and columns, with subtotals where they meet?
explanation: Matrix. It groups by rows and columns and totals up where they cross.
whyWrong: Tabular is just a flat list, no grouped subtotals at all.
Joined puts multiple report types side by side, it doesn't build the row-and-column grid a Matrix report does.
Summary groups rows and subtotals them, but not at row-and-column intersections like Matrix does.
